text.en: Break a chalk stick into smaller and smaller pieces and grind it. Can we keep breaking it forever?

Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space, and everything around us is made of matter.
Matter is made of tiny particles that are too small to see, even with a simple microscope.
In a solid the particles are tightly packed in fixed positions and can only vibrate.
In a liquid they are close but can slide over each other, so a liquid takes the shape of its container.
In a gas they are far apart and move freely in all directions, so a gas fills its container.
There are spaces between particles, which is why sugar dissolves in water without raising the level much.
Particles move on their own: the smell of food spreads across a room by diffusion, and ink spreads in water.
Diffusion is faster in gases than liquids and faster in warm substances because particles move faster when hot.
Particles attract each other, and this attraction is strongest in solids and weakest in gases.
The particle idea explains expansion on heating, change of state and why gases can be compressed.

problem.en: Why does the smell of incense spread across a room?

text.en: Particles of the scent move in all directions.
They mix with the air by diffusion.

prompt.en: Explain why a gas fills its whole container.

requiredIdeas.en: They move freely in all directions.
So they spread to fill the space.

points.en: Matter is made of tiny moving particles with spaces between them.
Solids, liquids and gases differ in how particles are arranged.
Diffusion shows particles move and is faster when warm.
